equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at 20x annualised NCI profit share (~EUR140M/yr)
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 NCI profit 77, FY2025 128; book NCI equity 711 at 2026-06-30. See inputs.nci_treatment.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 run-rate: 9M 2026 revenue 22,308 (+6.8% reported; Q1 +10.8%, H1 +9.7%, Q3 +7.2% at constant FX) against a Q4 2025 comp of +18.4% cFX, giving FY2026 ~+6.5% reported; consistent with management's 2026-2030 'solid growth' outlook. Equity CAGR rejected as the guide: EL pays out most of its earnings (dividends EUR1.3-1.8bn + buybacks) and its EUR39bn equity is dominated by merger goodwill, so book value compounds at 1-4% while owner FCF compounded at 6.8%/8.3%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.8% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 14.6% diverges >30% -- but both are distorted: the FY2020 base is the COVID trough (revenue -17%, EPS 0.19) and FY2021 consolidates GrandVision. The FY2019-based 6yr revenue CAGR of 8.6% and the 3yr figures (revenue 5.2%, owner FCF 6.8%) are the usable history.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF - lease principal - SBC, EUR M): FY2019 1,671; FY2020 1,686; FY2021 2,633; FY2022 2,065; FY2023 2,199; FY2024 2,250; FY2025 2,516. SBC rose from 162 (FY2024) to 280 (FY2025), so the owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (6.8%) is ABOVE the reported 5.5% only because FY2022's lease principal was unusually high (955 on first full GrandVision year); on the 5yr view owner FCF (8.3%) lags reported (10.3%) -- SBC and lease cash are growing faster than reported FCF. H1 2026 SBC fell to 135 from 165, so FY2025's 280 looks like a peak-grant year rather than a new level.

scenario_narratives.base: EssilorLuxottica is a vertically integrated vision-care utility with a consumer-electronics option attached. The base case pays for the utility -- recurring prescription demand, 18,000 stores, licensed-brand frames -- growing mid-single digits in EUR, with wearables and med-tech adding a point or two of growth that fades over the decade. Margin recovers to the pre-tariff 2022-24 level and stops; management's five-year outlook ('adjusted operating profit growth broadly aligned with revenue') promises nothing more. No net-cash, so no interest-income strip; leases are an operating cost and lease liabilities are not debt.
scenario_narratives.bull: The axes are (1) AI glasses becoming a mass category rather than a fad -- unit growth re-accelerating off the $299 tier and the prescription-first Optics line, (2) myopia management (Stellest, +22-24% growth) scaling in the US post-FDA, (3) med-tech/clinic roll-up creating a third leg, and (4) operating leverage restoring the 19-20% adjusted operating margin ambition. All four are independent; the bull case needs most of them.
scenario_narratives.bear: The axes are (1) wearables decelerating to zero under privacy regulation and Meta concentration risk, (2) tariffs and EUR strength as permanent margin and translation headwinds (65% of adjusted operating profit is USD-linked), (3) antitrust enforcement on a near-dominant position, and (4) a consumer slowdown hitting the discretionary sun/fashion-frame half of the business. None threatens solvency (ND/EBITDA 2.0x incl. leases, 75% fixed-rate debt), so the bear is a de-rating to a 3%-growth 23%-EBITDA-margin business, not distress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the recurring vision-care cash flows on a strict owner basis: SBC expensed, the full lease cash cost charged inside EBITDA (lease liabilities therefore excluded from net debt), minorities deducted at an earnings multiple, cash tax on an EBIT that excludes non-deductible PPA amortisation, and working capital charged against growth. Discount in EUR at a single 7.5% WACC; let the three scenarios and their weights carry the tariff, wearables and regulatory risk rather than the discount rate. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon and 20x FCF (16x bear). The market at ~36x trailing EPS has been paying for the AI-glasses option; the base case prices the utility and lets the bull scenario carry the option.
key_risks_to_valuation: Meta concentration: the fastest-growing product line depends on one partner's hardware roadmap, AI strategy and willingness to keep EL as exclusive frame/lens/retail partner; Meta's ~3% stake in EL adds governance ambiguity
Wearables deceleration already visible (near-100% to +20% YoY in Q3 2026); European privacy regulators (EDPB, Norway, Italy, Austria) and Australian workplace bans could cap adoption
US tariffs and USD weakness: ~65% of adjusted operating profit is USD-linked; FY2025 adjusted operating margin fell 100bp on tariffs and wearables mix, and the base case assumes most of that reverses

Antitrust/competition enforcement on a near-dominant integrated position (French fines EUR206M upheld, FTC and EU-country investigations open) could force commercial changes in lens distribution or retail

M&A-led med-tech build-out (Heidelberg, Optegra, Signifeye, Top Charoen, Supreme) carries integration and returns risk and is funded with debt while EUR1.7bn dividends and ~EUR1bn buybacks continue; ND/EBITDA rose to 2.0x at June 2026
Lease treatment: valuation assumes the 3.85%-of-revenue lease cost is permanent operating cost; if store-led DTC grows faster than revenue the bear's 4% is closer to the truth
NCI valued at 20x earnings (EUR2.8bn) rather than book (EUR0.7bn): roughly EUR4.5/share of judgment

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close, Euronext Paris); 52-week range 138.3-323.8
data_sources.financials: EL.PA_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2018-FY2025 annual, H1 2019-H1 2026 interim, EUR millions, from the Universal Registration Documents and Interim Financial Reports); H1 2026 Interim Financial Report for the 2026-06-30 net debt (note 15.3), share count (note 14) and diluted share data (note 8); FY2025 URD for lease principal (970), lease interest (126), ROU depreciation (993), PPA amortisation (830) and the adjusted P&L reconciliation; Q3 2026 revenue (EUR7.49bn, +7.2% cFX) from the 2026-10-20 release as summarised in EL.PA_Analysis.json
data_sources.qualitative: EL.PA_Analysis.json (bull/bear cases, growth drivers, guidance, recent developments) and the Outlook section of the H1 2026 Interim Financial Report (p.23: 2026-2030 'solid growth' in revenue with 'broadly aligned' adjusted operating profit growth, at constant FX)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-06-30: 464,247,548 issued less 4,655,973 treasury = 459,591,575 outstanding, plus 3,228,812 dilutive performance shares/options (diluted less basic weighted average, H1 2026 note 8) = 462.8M. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged; buybacks (EUR969M in H1 2026, 4.56M shares) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat. Scrip-dividend issuance (0.96M shares in 2026, 5.6M in 2025) is not modelled as growth: it is a dividend paid in paper, value-neutral to the DCF.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Company-defined FCF FY2025 = OCF 5,291 - capex 1,525 - lease principal 970 = 2,796 (FY2025 URD, Free Cash Flow reconciliation). The Metrics.csv free_cash_flow of 3,766 is pre-lease-principal; the lease principal is deducted here because leases are treated as an operating cost (treatment B).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD consolidated cash flow statement, 'Expense arising from share-based payments' EUR280M (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). Equity-award taxes: none disclosed (French/Italian performance-share plans settle gross; no net-share-settlement tax line), recorded as 0. Interest income (EUR75M FY2025) NOT deducted: the company is a net debtor (ND/EBITDA 2.0x incl. leases), so there is no cash pile being double-counted.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchases of treasury shares EUR376M net (CSV); H1 2026 EUR969M (4.56M shares, 2026 program up to 5M shares). Repurchaser: the flat count is being funded in cash.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:16Z regular close (Euronext Paris); three sessions after the Q3 2026 print (+11% on the day), not an after-hours quote
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of the statements and ~all of the debt. Risk-free: 10y Bund ~2.7% / OAT ~3.3%; ERP 5.5%; beta ~0.9 (diversified, largely non-discretionary vision-care demand, low-moderate cyclicality) -> cost of equity ~8.0%. After-tax cost of debt ~2.7% (bonds 2.5-3.5% coupon, 75% fixed). Market leverage ~10% (ND 9.5bn ex-leases vs ~84bn equity) -> WACC 7.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: tariff, wearables, Meta-dependence and regulatory risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full lease cash cost (FY2025 principal 970 + interest on lease liabilities 126 = 1,096, 3.85% of revenue; FY2024 1,052, 3.97%) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (EUR3,907M at 2026-06-30) are EXCLUDED from net debt, which is borrowings 11,409 less cash 1,931 = 9,478 (the company's own 'Net debt excluding lease liabilities'). D&A for cash-tax EBIT therefore excludes right-of-use depreciation (993 in FY2025) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI charged once, in the equity bridge, at 20x annualised NCI profit share (FY2025 128, FY2024 132, FY2023 137, H1 2026 77 -> ~140/yr x 20 = EUR2,800M). Book value of NCI (EUR711M at 2026-06-30) would understate the ~5% of group earnings that minorities own; 20x matches the terminal cap multiple so the minority is valued on the same basis as the parent.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is EBITDA BEFORE SBC and before lease cost, on the statutory (not 'adjusted') basis, so recurring restructuring/M&A costs the company labels non-GAAP (FY2025 249, FY2024 ~100, H1 2026 40) stay in the cost base. FY2025: (6,492 reported EBITDA + 280 SBC) / 28,491 = 23.8%; FY2024 25.3%; FY2023 25.0%; FY2022 25.8%; H1 2026 27.1% vs H1 2025 26.6% (H1 is seasonally the stronger half; H2 2025 ran ~21.1% on tariffs, wearables mix and the 249 of one-offs).
inputs.da_tax_basis: da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation AND ex purchase-price-allocation amortisation (FY2025: 3,113 total - 993 ROU - 830 PPA = 1,290 = 4.5% of revenue). EBIT so built ties to adjusted operating profit less lease interest less recurring 'non-GAAP' costs (FY2025 check: 5,396 owner EBITDA - 1,290 = 4,106 vs 4,459 - 126 - 249 = 4,084). PPA amortisation on merger intangibles/goodwill is largely non-deductible, so excluding it from the tax base is the right cash-tax model. Cash tax rate 21% -> 22%: cash taxes paid FY2022-25 averaged EUR900M against ~EUR4.25bn average adjusted PBT (21%); adjusted ETR 22.8-24.0% and management guides FY2026 slightly above 24%, so the path ramps up rather than holding the low FY2025 cash year (764).
inputs.working_capital_basis: wc_capture negative: manufacturer + retailer with inventories and receivables well above payables. Trade working capital rose EUR722M in H1 2026 on wearables; FY2023-25 WC & other absorbed ~15-35% of the revenue increase (FY2024 -397 on +1,113; FY2023 -145 on +901; FY2025 -85 on +1,983). Base -15% of the YoY revenue change.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, non-US, consumer/industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations for EUR WACC, IFRS 16 leases, NCI). Fresh build, no prior DCF or memory entry. Historical base is FY2019 onward: FY2018 consolidated Essilor for only three months (share count 266M vs ~440M later) and is not comparable. FY2021 investing cash flow included ~EUR7.1bn for GrandVision, a one-off excluded from the capex history. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec-2025) with FY2026 as projection year 1; the balance sheet is the later 2026-06-30 one, which already reflects the EUR1,728M dividend and EUR969M buyback paid in H1 2026 out of cash that year-1 FCF also counts -- a mild conservatism against shareholders, not a double-credit. Year-1 owner-FCF margin sanity: base FY2026 ~10.2% of revenue against an unlevered FY2025 equivalent of 9.6% (2,516 owner FCF + 226 net interest paid = 2,742) and FY2024 9.2%; the lift is the EBITDA recovery from the FY2025 trough (+60bp) and a normal tax year, both evidenced by H1 2026 (+50bp adjusted margin YoY, 24% ETR). Interest income not stripped (net debtor). SBC is small (1% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow but non-zero. Terminal cap 20x base/bull (quality compounder, Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% is 20.5x so the cap binds marginally), 16x bear (structurally slower).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and quote both EUR; no conversion. ~76% of revenue is non-EUR (~65% of adjusted operating profit USD-linked), so EUR strength depresses reported growth: H1 2026 +9.7% cFX vs +5.7% reported; Q3 2026 +7.2% cFX vs ~+9% reported as the comp eased. Growth paths below are in reported EUR.

bear.narrative: Wearables growth, already down from ~100% to 20% in Q3 2026, stalls as European privacy regulators (EDPB, Norway, Italy, Austria) restrict use and Meta diversifies suppliers or squeezes terms; the category becomes a low-margin accessory rather than a platform. US tariffs stay, EUR stays strong, and competition/antitrust enforcement (French fines upheld, FTC and EU probes open) caps pricing power in lenses and retail. Revenue grows ~3% (core vision care only), EBITDA (pre-SBC) settles at 23%, below FY2025's 23.8%, lease and capex intensity drift up as store-led DTC growth outruns revenue. Terminal cap 16x for a structurally slower business.

base.narrative: Growth: FY2026 +6.5% (9M run-rate), then mid-single-digit decelerating to 3%: core vision care at market (~4-5%), wearables growing but no longer doubling, bolt-on clinic/retail M&A inside the capex/WC envelope. Margin: EBITDA (pre-SBC) recovers from the FY2025 tariff/wearables trough of 23.8% to 25.8%, i.e. back to the FY2022-24 range and no further -- management's own 'adjusted operating profit growth broadly aligned with revenue' framing promises no expansion. Implied terminal adjusted operating margin ~17% (25.8 - 0.8 SBC - 3.85 lease - 4.5 D&A + 0.45 lease interest) vs 15.7% FY2025 and 16.7% FY2024.

bull.narrative: AI glasses become a durable category (IDC ~27M industry units by 2030, EL the dominant supplier), the $299 Meta Glasses tier broadens the funnel, Stellest's FDA authorisation turns myopia management into a US growth engine, and the Optegra/Signifeye/Top Charoen clinic-and-retail roll-up compounds. Operating leverage on wearables scale and tariff pass-through lifts EBITDA (pre-SBC) to 28%, i.e. the formerly targeted 19-20% adjusted operating margin. Lease intensity eases slightly as e-commerce and subscriptions take share from stores.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the 15/50/35 default to 20/50/30. Bull weight down because it needs several independent things to go right at once (wearables re-acceleration AND margin expansion AND tariff relief) and the Q3 2026 wearables deceleration to +20% is direct evidence against the first. Bear weight up to 20% for the Meta single-partner dependency, live European privacy scrutiny of AI glasses, and the FY2025 margin dilution showing tariffs and wearables mix can bite -- but not higher, because there is no going-concern or covenant risk and the core vision-care franchise is non-discretionary.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
